segments: ... intelligent, learned in books, and famous in every subject.
And when Abd al-Malik, king of the Arabs, heard of his reputation,
he sent and summoned him.
And seeing that he was competent in everything,
he sent him with the youth Abd al-Aziz, his brother, to Egypt,
and entrusted to him the administration of the young man.
And he rose so high
that the entire kingdom of the Arabs was administered through his hands.
And he grew and became very rich,
and acquired four thousand slaves,
and estates, villages, and herds (or estates),
and gold and silver like stones.
And from the income of four hundred shops which he possessed in Edessa,
he ordered and built a magnificent temple of the Mother of God.
He also built two large temples in Fustat, the city in Egypt.
And he also built a baptistery in Edessa,
and placed in it that image of Christ which had been sent to King Abgar.
And he made for it a water basin, just as Bishop Amazonius {OCR?} had made in the old church of Edessa,
and adorned it with gold and silver plated with bronze.
This Athanasius was envied by a certain Chalcedonian scribe of Damascus named Sergius bar Mansur.
And when the emir Abd al-Aziz died,
and Athanasius left Egypt,
Sergius denounced him and said:
"Bar Gumaye has plundered the treasuries of Egypt and brought them with him."
King Abd al-Malik, however,
did not even then become angry with Athanasius,
but said to him peaceably:
"It is not right that all this wealth should belong to the Christians;
give us a portion of it."
Athanasius readily consented,
and gave until the king himself said:
"It is enough."
And much more remained for him.
And in the year 1015 [AD 703/704],
Abd al-Malik sent Maslamah,
and he captured Mopsuestia.
And in the same year, the Arabs of Kufa and of Basra rebelled,
and fought with Abd al-Malik.
And in it also, Justinian escaped from exile,
and fled to the Khagan, king of the Khazars, who welcomed him.
And he gave him his daughter in marriage,
and she bore him a son {OCR?}, and he named him Tiberius.
And having received an army from the Khagan and from the Bulgars,
he came against Constantinople {OCR?}.
And Apsimar fled.
And Justinian reigned again for six years after
